newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Raiders attack French oil facility in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Raiders attack French oil facility in Colombia.

text.p: Heavily-armed raiders forced their way into an oil facility operated by French company Kelt Colombia SA in eastern Colombia and dynamited an electronic instrumentation panel, a company spokesman said Monday.
He denied local media reports that one of the company's wells had been blown up and said there had been no danger of an oil spill.

The plant at Los Toros, a community about 50 miles (80 km) from the town of Trinidad, in Casanare province, separates water from the crude coming from 11 wells in the area, reinjects water into the wells and pumps crude into a pipeline. The Kelt spokesman said the facility has a daily throughput of between 3,000 and 4,000 barrels per day.

The control panel, he said, was essentially a series of alarms that warned of potential faults in production and operating systems. It will take at least two months to repair but is not expected to affect production, the company official said.

Three men stormed into the plant about 1930 local Friday (0030 GMT Saturday), fired shots from high-powered rifles into the air and forced a small team of employees out of the building, the spokesman said.
In addition to blowing up the control panel, the intruders also placed a three pound (1.5 kg) dynamite charge in a compressor, which failed to explode.

"It was a very strange attack. This type of thing has never happened before. We're carrying out investigations but we cannot say whether it was guerrillas or anybody else at this stage," the spokesman said.
The National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest rebel force, specializes in attacks on oil infrastructure but generally limits attacks to pipelines.

Kelt works in partnership with Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol and U.S. firm Hocol SA. It operates a total of 15 wells in Casanare with a combined daily production of between 25,000 and 30,000 barrels per day.
Most of the wells Kelt now runs were formerly operated by French multinational Elf Aquitaine, which moved out as production became unprofitable.
